evidence: app/src/components/PokemonCard.tsx:17 — sprite URL built in exactly one place, so any URL fix covers every card list
app/src/lib/data.ts:56-66 — species index carries only {id, name}; default-variety sprite data is not in the card pipeline
app/src/lib/data.ts:173-184 — cardForSpeciesId builds cards for move/ability/type lists, while home items are built separately at data.ts:151-158
app/src/lib/data.ts:324-335 — getAbilityPage's dedup 'seen' logic; getMovePage at 298-304 lacks it (same job, drift between copies)
changeability.rationale: Rendering fixes land in one obvious component, but a data-shape fix touches two duplicated card builders and must first thread new data through the species index; pervasive 'any' typing means the compiler won't flag any of it.

evidence: app/src/routes/api-proxy/[...path].ts:3-5, app/src/routes/media/[...path].ts:3-5 — API base URL isolated behind server proxies; client code never knows it
app/src/lib/api.ts:26-45 — single client fetch/cache seam every data function goes through
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:96,113 — route reaches into raw payload (species.id, pokemon.height) instead of transformed fields
app/src/routes/moves/[name].tsx:41-43 — route reads data().move.damage_class directly, bypassing getMovePage's transform layer
app/src/lib/data.ts — 430 lines holding all five pages' data logic in one module
coupling.rationale: Server/client and component/data seams are genuinely clean, but routes mix raw 'any' payloads with transformed fields (leaky boundary), and the single god-module data layer means every cross-page change funnels through one file.

evidence: app/src/components/PokemonCard.tsx:9-13,27 — typed CardData with optional types/hidden stretches to home, move, ability and type lists without duplication
app/src/components/MoveTable.tsx:12-22 — MoveRow interface plus includeLevel flag; sorting logic (62-111) is self-contained and reusable
app/src/lib/data.ts:298-304,324-335,353-364 — the fetch→englishName→effect→card-list pattern is copy-pasted per resource rather than parameterized
app/src/lib/data.ts:124,298,322,353 — speciesById Map rebuilt identically in four places
app/src/components/PokemonCard.tsx:24,36 — showTypes prop and hidden flag are mild but justified flag creep around real variation
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared components are well designed around real variation, but the resource-page data layer has no abstraction at all: an Items section would clone getMovePage's ~40 lines rather than reuse a parameterized resource helper.

findings.issue: Card-list construction (fetch→dedup id≤10000→cardForSpeciesId→sort by id) is copy-pasted in getMovePage, getAbilityPage and getTypePage with drift: the 'seen' dedup exists in two copies but not the third, and speciesById is rebuilt at data.ts:298, 322 and 353.
findings.suggestion: Extract one helper, e.g. pokemonCardsFromRefs(refs: NamedRef[]): Promise<Card[]>, built on a shared cached species index, and call it from all three page functions.

findings.issue: The entire data layer is typed 'any' (species, pokemon, move, ability are all any), and routes also reach into raw payloads (app/src/routes/moves/[name].tsx:41-43, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:96,113), so API shape changes surface as runtime errors, not compile errors.
findings.suggestion: Define payload interfaces for the handful of API resources used, or at least type the returned page-data objects so routes consume transformed, typed fields only.

findings.issue: One 430-line module owns data logic for all five pages; every cross-page change (sorting, card shape, cache rules) funnels through it and merge conflicts/concept load grow with each feature.
findings.suggestion: Split per resource (data/species.ts, data/moves.ts, …) sharing api.ts and format.ts; the existing module-level promise memos move with their owner.

findings.issue: The API_BASE env resolution is defined twice; changing the base-URL rule means editing both.
findings.suggestion: Move a single exported apiBaseUrl() into app/src/lib (shared server-side constant) and import it in both proxies.

findings.issue: Two independent caches with different rules: api.ts TTL cache (60s) plus permanent module-level promise memos in data.ts; changing caching policy means reasoning about both layers, and the memos never expire.
findings.suggestion: Have the data-layer memos delegate to apiGet's cache (or fold TTL policy into one place) so cache rules are stated once.

findings.issue: The loading-fallback + NotFound nested Show pattern is repeated almost verbatim in four route files.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small <DataPage> wrapper (resource → loading shell | NotFound | content) so page routes shrink to content.

findings.issue: HomeData exposes speciesById, typesByPokemon and generationBySpecies maps that no route consumes — speculative surface a maintainer must keep working.
findings.suggestion: Keep them module-local and return only {items, generations, types}.

findings.issue: Home page maps over pageItems() with array .map instead of <For>, inconsistent with every other list in the app; Solid's For avoids re-creating DOM nodes on page/filter changes.
findings.suggestion: Use <For each={pageItems()}> for consistency and Solid-recommended keyed rendering.

findings.issue: document.documentElement.lang is set in a client effect even though entry-server.tsx already emits <html lang="en"> — redundant mutation on every boot.
findings.suggestion: Delete the effect and rely on the server shell's lang attribute.

summary: A clean, idiomatic SolidStart v2 layout (proxy-isolated data source, typed presentational components, single fetch seam) that is pleasant to modify at the route/component level but weakly factored at the data layer: a 430-line any-typed module whose per-resource functions are copy-pasted with drift. Most fixes land in one rendering component; most data-shape changes land in three or four places with no compiler safety net. Solid mid-range editability.
